title: San Francisco Home Energy Rebates 2026: What CleanPowerSF Pays | HomePowerRebate
desc: San Francisco home rebates in 2026: CleanPowerSF bill credits for heat pumps and water heaters up to $1,200 each, electric cooking and dryers, plus what is left for solar and batteries.
badge: Up to $1,200 each for heating and hot water
lead: San Francisco's electricity supplier is CleanPowerSF, run by the SFPUC, and almost everything it offers for homes comes as monthly bill credits, not cash. Hot water and heating earn the most. Solar cash rebates have mostly ended. We read CleanPowerSF's pages on October 2, 2026.
cards_intro: Each card links to a page with the rules and the local detail. All credits are $50 a month, and the hot water and heating credits need an electrification rate such as EV2-A or E-ELEC.

sections: CleanPowerSF pays $50 off your bill each month. A heat pump water heater earns 24 of them, which is $1,200, and CARE or FERA customers get 12 more. Credits stop if you move, so the program favors people who stay. Because the money arrives slowly, a project quote that counts the full $1,200 as an up-front discount is wrong. Ask your installer how they treat it.

You must be a residential CleanPowerSF customer, comply with the Department of Building Inspection's permit rules, use a model from the approved products list, and apply online. For hot water and heating, you must also be on an electrification rate such as EV2-A or E-ELEC. The City takes plumbing and mechanical permits through PermitSF, where contractors need an eligible license.
What San Francisco does not offer

We found no CleanPowerSF rebate for insulation, windows or an EV charger for homes, though it lists an EV Charge SF program for financing charging infrastructure with up to $120,000 in incentives and a $1,000 e-bike coupon for 1,000 customers. Those are outside our home rebate categories, so we link to them without counting them. If you find a current home program we missed, tell us at hello@homepowerrebate.com.

BayREN's EASE Home program pays 80% of weatherization costs for income-qualified PG&E customers in the Bay Area, and helps with applications (BayREN). The federal 25C and 25D tax credits ended after December 31, 2025. TECH Clean California and the federal HEEHRA program are fully reserved for single-family homes and take new requests on hold only.

San Francisco's credits are smaller and slower than the cash amounts in Glendale (Glendale), LADWP territory (Los Angeles) and SMUD territory (Sacramento). Its strength is that it rewards a whole-home switch, adding $300 when the gas meter comes out. San Francisco's average January low over 2015 to 2024 was 7.8°C, so heating needs are small.
installers_intro: These San Francisco heat pump and HVAC companies have the best Google ratings, listed by rating and then review count. We are not paid to list anyone. CleanPowerSF keeps an Active Contractors List, so ask whether your installer is on it.
claim_steps: Look at your electric bill and confirm that CleanPowerSF supplies your power.
Pick the upgrade that fits your next purchase and open its page for the rules.
If you want hot water or heating credits, move your account to an electrification rate such as EV2-A or E-ELEC.
Hire a licensed contractor and ask who pulls the City permit.
Apply for bill credits online after the work is done.
faq: Who supplies electricity in San Francisco?
CleanPowerSF, run by the SFPUC, supplies electricity, and PG&E delivers it. Its rebates are separate from PG&E's.
Heat pump water heaters and heat pump heating each earn up to $1,200. A gas meter removal adds $300.
Are the credits paid all at once?
No. They are $50 a month on your bill, for 24 months for hot water and heating, and shorter periods for cooking and dryers.
Is there a solar rebate in San Francisco?
GoSolarSF now pays only low-income customers. The CleanPowerSF battery program, up to $3,750, is marked coming soon.
Can I get help if my income is limited?
CARE and FERA customers get 12 extra months of credits on hot water and heating, and BayREN's EASE Home pays 80% of weatherization for income-qualified PG&E customers.
